story.title: iPhone Lockdown Mode: The Pros And Cons Of Enabling Apple's Security Feature - Engadget

facts.text: If Lockdown Mode sounds aggressive, it's because that's exactly what it was designed for.
Back in 2023, an exploit known as "Blastpass" used iMessage to install the Pegasus spyware on Apple devices .
However, researchers found that devices in Lockdown Mode were completely immune to the spyware.
Apple offers a 100 percent bonus on top of the regular reward through its Security Bounty program to anyone who finds a way to bypass the feature, which shows how much the company trusts it.
By restricting your iPhone to avoid potential attack vectors, you're given maximum security in exchange for reduced functionality and convenience.
The iPhone's Lockdown Mode has been around since 2022 , but you might not have heard about it, let alone used it.
Apple itself calls the tool an "extreme" layer of security for the few people who may be targeted by commercial spyware such as NSO's Pegasus .
Journalists, activists and politicians are among the potential targets of such spyware.
Anyone with an iPhone running iOS 16 or newer can try out Lockdown Mode.
It's also available on iPadOS 16 and later, watchOS 10 and newer, and macOS 13 Ventura and later.
To turn it on, open Settings and go to Privacy & Security .
Scroll down until you find Lockdown Mode , then tap Turn On & Restart and confirm with your passcode.
It's simple as that, and you'll find the option to disable it in the same place.
However, many of those features are ones you likely use every day.
In Messages, most kinds of attachments are blocked.
Even link previews stop working, since they can serve as a backdoor for spyware.
Lockdown Mode also restricts how JavaScript works in browsers, which may cause some websites to load slowly or not work at all.
FaceTime calls are also blocked; only people you've called recently can reach you.
For most people, there's no need to use Lockdown Mode.
Apple devices already have many security and privacy features built in.
Spyware like Pegasus usually targets public figures and is often deployed by governments that want to spy on opponents or protesters.
Chances are that the inconveniences it creates are not worth the extreme level of protection that few people need.
For instance, wired connections are disabled when the device is locked — meaning it cannot communicate with a computer or accessory without your passcode.

For wireless connectivity, your iPhone will no longer automatically connect to unsecured networks, and support for 2G and 3G networks is completely disabled (though these networks were discontinued in the US years ago).
If you have an Apple Watch, phone call notifications from your iPhone won't show up on it.

I put my Pixel into lockdown mode every night before bed, and again every time I left the house for a week.l The first couple of days took a little cognitive effort to remember to do it, but typing the PIN in to unlock was like revisiting an old friend.
I was fully ok with it after day three; it just felt like the biometrics weren't working and typing in the 6-digit number was seamless (fine, i forgot a couple of times, sheesh).
The only friction was the Lock Screen Notification suppression, to be honest.
I've come to rely on those to let me know what's happening on my phone without having to open it up.
Still, it's a much stronger security feature , especially if I'm at a protest (I live in Portland, so that's fairly often).
It's something I wish my iPhone had going for it.
My OnePlus Open doesn't have a lockdown mode, either.
Lockdown mode asks very little of me: a simple button press, tap, then unlock with a PIN.
The protection it offers against compelled biometric access is real and unfortunately fairly relevant lately here in the U.S. at least.
If you have a Pixel and travel or hit a protest or two, this is worth making a habit.
The fastest way to enable lockdown mode on a Google Pixel is by pressing the Volume up and Power buttons .
You'll see a slider to Power off your iPhone, one to bring up your Medical ID, and one to activate an SOS Emergency Call.
If you hit Cancel, your iPhone will require your pass code before going back to FaceID mode.
Before you come at me, though, and say "this is the same thing as Pixel," I'll respectfully disagree.
There's nothing clear about the iOS solution, even if functionally it does similar.
Lockdown on Pixel actually locks your phone immediately, no Cancel button needed.
Lockdown mode resets automatically on the next unlock.
The Google Pixel 10a is a budget-oriented smartphone with a flat back and long battery life.
It's powered by the same Tensor G4 chip as its predecessor, and many key specs are identical to the Pixel 9a.
However, you do get a brighter screen, better modem, new software features, and Android 16 with seven years of software support.
The best of MakeUseOf, directly in your inbox.
Don't forget about repair mode too - locks your internal files down until you unlock it with a passcode - added security
